features.name: Service list discovery
features.summary: The registry answers queries with schema-valid Service List Entry Points for every offering type, includes offerings that leave a filter unspecified, refuses invalid TargetCountry and Language values, writes the service list media type and @regulatorListFlag, refuses unknown genre terms, and serves over TLS when configured, otherwise plain HTTP with a warning; how it treats image_variant falls under a contradiction in the specification. The browser client queries a registry, lists regulator lists first, acts on Delivery, Language, TargetCountry and logos, makes a regulator list the default whenever there is one, and checks ServiceListId. The Exo DVB-I Player does no discovery of its own.

requirements.name: Service List Registry query filtering

cases.case: Query endpoint answers an HTTP GET
cases.what: Serves GET /query and answers a valid query with 200 and a ServiceListEntryPoints XML document built from the registry's stored offerings.

cases.case: No filtering on a parameter that is absent
cases.what: Each filter (TargetCountry, Delivery, Language, Genre, regulatorListFlag, ProviderName) is applied only when the parameter is present, so a query without parameters returns every offering.

cases.case: Repeated values with square bracket notation are alternatives (OR)
cases.what: Reads a parameter whether sent once or repeated as name[]=, and keeps an offering if any one of the values matches.

cases.case: TargetCountry query includes offerings that specify no TargetCountry
cases.what: The TargetCountry filter is applied only to an offering that declares at least one country, so an offering with no TargetCountry is included in the results of any TargetCountry query.

cases.case: Language query includes offerings that specify no Language
cases.what: The Language filter is applied only to an offering that declares at least one language, so an offering with no Language is included in the results of any Language query.

cases.case: Genre query includes offerings that specify no Genre
cases.what: The Genre filter is applied only to an offering that declares at least one genre, so an offering with no Genre is included in the results of any Genre query.

cases.case: Delivery query values and their DeliveryTypes (table 12b)
cases.what: Accepts exactly dvb-dash, dvb-t, dvb-c, dvb-s, dvb-iptv and application, matching dvb-dash on DASHDelivery, dvb-iptv on MulticastTSDelivery or RTSPDelivery, and the others on their own DeliveryType; an offering matches only on a DeliveryType it actually emits, so one declared without its mandatory values does not match.

cases.case: regulatorListFlag query
cases.what: With regulatorListFlag=true only offerings marked as the regulator's list are returned, with false only the others, and without the parameter both.

cases.case: ProviderName query
cases.what: Keeps only providers whose name equals one of the ProviderName values, compared without regard to case.

noted: Different parameters narrow the result together (each must match); the clause gives the OR rule for repeated values only.
Language values in the query are lower-cased before comparison, while stored values are compared as written, so an offering stored with an upper-case language code never matches.

A TargetCountry value is read as a comma separated list (the type allows several codes) and each code, on the query and on the offering, is an alternative; no clause defines matching for a list value.

Only the first regulatorListFlag value is used, so a query repeating the flag with true and false returns only one kind of list; the clause applies the OR rule where multiple values are accepted and does not say whether they are for this boolean.
A request URL longer than 2 048 characters is answered with 414; the clause sets the limit but names no response.
Genre is used to filter but is never written into the response, so a client cannot see why an offering matched a Genre query.

Delivery values are compared without regard to case, so a value such as DVB-DASH is accepted and matched although table 12b lists the values in lower case; the clause does not say whether case matters.

requirements.name: Service List Registry error responses

cases.case: 400 for an undefined query parameter
cases.what: Any parameter other than the seven clause 5.1.3.2 lists, with or without square brackets, is answered with 400.

cases.case: image_variant query parameter
cases.what: image_variant is not one of the accepted parameters, so a request carrying it is answered with 400 whatever its value, including a value listed in table 8.
cases.conflict: TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 5.2.8.2.1: "The list of image_variant query parameters listed in table 8 shall be used by ALL endpoints to validate image_variant query parameters." and "If a valid value from this list is used, the response shall not error but is not required to contain an image." Clause 5.1.3.2 does not list image_variant among the Service List Registry parameters and requires 400 "if an undefined query parameter is provided with a request to a Service List Registry endpoint; or".

cases.case: 400 for an invalid Delivery value
cases.what: A Delivery value outside table 12b is answered with 400.

cases.case: 400 for an invalid regulatorListFlag or inlineImages value
cases.what: A value other than true or false is answered with 400.

cases.case: 400 for an invalid TargetCountry value
cases.what: Every TargetCountry value must match the ISO-3166-List pattern of its schema type (upper-case three-letter codes, comma separated), or the query is answered with 400; lower-case and malformed codes are refused.
cases.locator: clause 5.1.3.2; clause 5.3.5 (TargetCountry of type tva:ISO-3166-List); tva_metadata_3-1.xsd, simpleType ISO-3166-List, pattern [A-Z]{3}(,[A-Z]{3})*

cases.case: 400 for an invalid Language value
cases.what: Every Language value must match the lexical pattern of the XML Schema language type on which the Language type is based, or the query is answered with 400.
cases.locator: clause 5.1.3.2; clause 5.3.5 (Language of type tva:AudioLanguageType); tva_metadata_3-1.xsd AudioLanguageType, tva_mpeg7.xsd ExtendedLanguageType (base language); XML Schema Part 2 Second Edition clause 3.3.3

cases.case: 400 for an invalid Genre value
cases.what: A Genre value is refused with 400 unless it is one of the three table 12 scheme URIs followed by a colon and a term identifier that the loaded scheme files define; the registry does not start without those files, so a well-formed value naming a term no scheme defines is always refused.

noted: The registry requires no query parameter, so the 422 response for a registry that does never arises.
A parameter given with an empty value is treated as absent rather than refused.
regulatorListFlag and inlineImages accept true and false in any letter case and refuse 1 and 0; the clause calls the values boolean but does not say which written forms a query may use.

TS 103 770 V1.2.1 is not consistent on this: clause 5.1.3.2 requires 400 for an undefined parameter, while clause 6.2.2 says a server may ignore it. Answering 400 satisfies both, so the verdict does not depend on which reading applies.

TargetCountry and Language values are checked against the patterns of their schema types only; whether a code is in the ISO 3166 list or is a registered language identifier is not checked (ISO 3166 and RFC 3066 not held for this audit).

The form of a Genre value (scheme URI, a colon, the term identifier) is a reading: clause 5.1.3.2 does not define it, and the rule for term references is in ISO/IEC 15938-5, not held. The repository tests use small synthetic schemes; the scheme file of clause D.5 from the TS 103 770 attachments loads with its 95 terms (observed, read-only, Node.js 24.19.0). The TV-Anytime ContentCS and FormatCS files are not held for this audit, so loading them was not observed and the test that reads the real files was not run.

requirements.name: Service List Registry query response

cases.case: Response is a ServiceListEntryPoints document valid against the clause 5.3 schema
cases.what: Returns ServiceListEntryPoints in the servicelistdiscovery 2024 namespace with xml:lang, then ProviderOffering elements; responses built from the shipped data and the test data, including offerings with DVB-C, DVB-S and application delivery, validate against dvbi_service_list_discovery_v1.6.xsd in the repository's schema check.

cases.case: No ProviderOffering when nothing matches
cases.what: A provider with no matching offering is left out, so a query that matches nothing returns a document with ServiceListRegistryEntity and no ProviderOffering.

noted: The response is served as application/xml; the specification defines no media type for it.

inlineImages is accepted and validated but changes nothing: the registry stores and emits no graphical element in any form (RelatedMaterial is optional), so there is nothing to inline and, without the parameter, the default of false is met.

requirements.name: Service List Entry Point fields

cases.case: ServiceListRegistryEntity
cases.what: Emits ServiceListRegistryEntity with the registry's Name; no Kind, contact or regulatorFlag is emitted, all optional.
cases.locator: clause 5.3.2, Table 9, row ServiceListRegistryEntity; clause 5.3.3, Table 10

cases.case: ProviderOffering with Provider and ServiceListOffering
cases.what: Each matching provider becomes one ProviderOffering with a Provider Name and one ServiceListOffering per matching offering.

cases.case: ServiceListName, Language, TargetCountry and ServiceListId
cases.what: Emits ServiceListName, Language, TargetCountry and ServiceListId from the stored offering, in schema order.

cases.case: ServiceListURI @contentType
cases.what: Every ServiceListURI carries contentType application/vnd.dvb.dvbisl+xml, the media type of a Service List.

cases.case: Delivery with DASHDelivery, DVBTDelivery, RTSPDelivery, MulticastTSDelivery
cases.what: Emits the declared DeliveryType children as empty elements in schema order, which is valid for these four types.

cases.case: Delivery with DVBCDelivery, DVBSDelivery or ApplicationDelivery
cases.what: DVBCDelivery is written with its networkID, DVBSDelivery with one or more OrbitalPosition values and ApplicationDelivery with one or more ApplicationType elements carrying contentType (and xmlAitApplicationType for an XML AIT), taken from the registry data and checked against their schema types; a delivery declared without valid values is left out and logged, so no incomplete element is written.
cases.locator: clause 5.3.6.6, Table 12f, row @networkID; clause 5.3.6.7, Table 12g, row OrbitalPosition; clause 5.3.6.8, Table 12h, row ApplicationType

cases.case: @regulatorListFlag on a regulator's list
cases.what: An offering stored as the regulator's list is written with regulatorListFlag="true"; other offerings leave the attribute out and so take the default false.

noted: @version is not emitted (it is optional), so a client cannot tell from the document that the registry data changed.
Several ServiceListName values can be emitted without xml:lang; Table 12 allows several names only with different xml:lang values.

ServiceListName and ServiceListId are whatever the operator stores; nothing compares them with the Name and id of the list at the ServiceListURI, which Table 12 requires to be the same name. With the shipped data and the provider's default configuration they differ.
The stored kind of the registry is not written into ServiceListRegistryEntity.
No offering is marked as carried over 5G Broadcast: TS 103 770 V1.2.1 gives a registry no element or Delivery value for it, and the registry adds none of its own.
No delivery type is ever marked @required (optional, default false), so a client cannot tell which delivery methods the provider considers essential.
No RelatedMaterial (service list logo) is emitted, and the registry data has no field for one; the element is optional.

SRSSupport is never emitted and the registry data has no field for it. TS 103 770 clause 5.6.4.1 places the duty to include SRSSupport in the ServiceListOffering on the Service List Server, while the ServiceListOffering is returned by the registry, so the specification does not say who emits it.
An offering that declares only deliveries without valid values is written with an empty Delivery element, which the schema allows; it then matches no Delivery query.

requirements.name: HTTP over TLS (registry)

cases.case: Query endpoint served over TLS
cases.what: With a key and certificate configured the registry serves its endpoints over HTTPS only, and an incomplete or unreadable TLS configuration stops it rather than falling back to HTTP. With neither configured it serves plain HTTP with a warning and does not check that clients are on its private subnet, while the clause allows HTTP without TLS only in that case. Serving plain HTTP with a warning follows an owner decision.

cases.case: Server supports TLS 1.2 (and should support TLS 1.3)
cases.what: The HTTPS server uses the runtime's default TLS range, TLS 1.2 to TLS 1.3, and refuses to start if the configured range excludes TLS 1.2, warning if it excludes TLS 1.3; handshakes with TLS 1.2 only and TLS 1.3 only both succeed in the repository test.

noted: The TLS profile the clause takes from ETSI TS 102 796 clause 11.2 (root certificates, cipher suites, signature algorithms, key sizes, curves) is not applied; the runtime defaults are used.
The shipped registry data lists the provider's service list at an http:// URL on localhost.

requirements.name: Client query to a Service List Registry

cases.case: Percent-encoding of query values
cases.what: The country code the user types is percent-encoded before it is put in the query, every reserved character of RFC 3986 clause 2.2 included (the gen-delims and the sub-delims ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =), with uppercase hexadecimal digits.

cases.case: Parameters in the specified order
cases.what: Sends a single parameter, TargetCountry, so the order rule is met; no other parameter and no repeated value is ever sent.

noted: The registry endpoint is user-configurable and defaults to a third-party public registry; a query string already in the configured endpoint is kept and TargetCountry appended after it.
Besides a registry, the client accepts a typed Service List URL, preset URLs and a built-in default URL, the other discovery options clause 5.1.3.1 describes.

The registry query goes through the same HTTP handling as the service list requests (clause 4.3, judged under its own feature): a failure is reported to the user as a failed lookup and not retried automatically, and after a 400 or 406 the same query is not sent again.
The character set of annex C of ETSI TS 102 809 that the clause also requires of query parameters is not checked: the value is sent as the user types it, upper-cased.

requirements.name: Client support of Service List Entry Point fields

cases.case: ServiceListEntryPoints and ProviderOffering (Tables 80, 82)
cases.what: Recognises a ServiceListEntryPoints root and reads every ServiceListOffering in it, in any namespace, using the Provider Name only as a fallback label.

cases.case: ServiceListName and ServiceListURI (Table 83)
cases.what: Labels each offering with its first ServiceListName and keeps all of its ServiceListURI addresses, in order and without duplicates, as fallbacks for the same list; a single installable offering is loaded at once, several are offered for the user to pick.
cases.locator: clause 8.5.3.2, Table 83, rows ServiceListName and ServiceListURI

cases.case: @regulatorListFlag preference (Table 83 note 2)
cases.what: Reads the flag and offers regulator lists first; whenever the response includes a regulator list the default is one: the first it can install, or, when none can be installed here, the first one, marked as the default but disabled with the reason shown. Without a regulator list the first list it can install is the default.

cases.case: Delivery and its DeliveryType children (Tables 83, 83a)
cases.what: Reads Delivery and each delivery type in it with its @required flag; an offering that requires a broadcast, RTSP or multicast delivery, or only application types this client cannot run, is shown disabled with the reason and is not installed, and several required DVB-T, DVB-C or DVB-S entries are taken as alternatives.

cases.case: Language and TargetCountry (Table 83)
cases.what: Reads Language and TargetCountry and shows them; offerings in the preferred audio language are offered first, and an offering whose TargetCountry does not include the country looked up is shown disabled; one without TargetCountry is accepted for any country.
cases.locator: clause 8.5.3.2, Table 83, rows Language and TargetCountry

cases.case: RelatedMaterial (Table 83)
cases.what: Reads the service list logo (HowRelatedCS:2021:1001.1) of each offering and shows it beside the offering name; a logo that fails to load is removed.

cases.case: Organization @regulatorFlag (Table 81)
cases.what: Reads @regulatorFlag of the registry entity and of each provider; the picker says when the registry is a recognized regulator and labels offerings whose provider is one.

noted: A response with no ServiceListOffering, which means nothing matched, is treated as if the registry URL were itself a Service List and is fetched again as one.
A non-standard root of ProviderOffering in the older servicediscovery namespaces is also parsed; it carries none of the fields above and they are not read from it.
ServiceListURI @contentType is ignored; any URI is fetched as a Service List.
When an offering has several ServiceListName values the first is shown, whatever the user's language preference.
Genre and SRSSupport, which table 83 does not mark for any receiver, are not read.

When the regulator list is the default but cannot be installed here (for example it requires DVB-S), it is shown as the default and disabled, so the user picks another list; NOTE 2 does not say what a client should do with a regulator list it cannot receive.

requirements.name: Client use of required delivery and ServiceListId

cases.case: Install only when every required delivery type is usable (should)
cases.what: Reads @required on every delivery type of an offering; an offering that requires a delivery this IP-only client cannot use (DVB-T, DVB-C, DVB-S, RTSP, multicast, or only application types it cannot run) is shown disabled with the reason and never installed, also when it is the only one returned. This is a should.

cases.case: ServiceList@id checked against ServiceListOffering ServiceListId (should)
cases.what: Keeps the registry's ServiceListId with the offering; a list whose @id differs fails like any other error, so the next ServiceListURI is tried and, when none works, the failure is reported with the mismatch as its cause. This is a should.

requirements.name: Service list discovery in the Exo DVB-I Player

cases.case: Query a Service List Registry and read ServiceListEntryPoints
cases.what: The wrapper sends no registry query and parses no ServiceListEntryPoints document; discovery and service list handling happen in the external third-party frontend it loads, which is not 5G-MAG code.

requirements.exists: A hard-coded landing page of the external frontend is loaded in the WebView, and a hard-coded Service List URL on the same third-party host is fetched into the app cache.
noted: The wrapper downloads one fixed Service List into its cache at start-up, but nothing in this repository reads that file.

features.name: Service lists and services
features.summary: The provider publishes schema-valid service lists as application/vnd.dvb.dvbisl+xml, with a new version on every change, JPEG or PNG logos, image variants, subscription packages, one LCN table per region and region selection by regionID. The client chooses one LCN table by region, honours @visible, @selectable and LCNRange, every target region, subscription packages, parental ratings and linked applications, and reads XML AITs; it does not apply the XML AIT platform profile, and when the XML AIT of an application offered beside the media has no application it can run, it hides the application rather than showing it as unavailable. The Exo player leaves all of this to an external frontend.

requirements.name: Service list publication (media type)

cases.case: Service list served at a stable URL
cases.what: Serves the generated ServiceList at one fixed URL on every GET, with Last-Modified and conditional GET.

cases.case: Media type application/vnd.dvb.dvbisl+xml
cases.what: Sends the service list with Content-Type application/vnd.dvb.dvbisl+xml.

noted: Whether the list is served over TLS (clause 7.3) is not judged in this feature.

requirements.name: Each service defined once in a list

cases.case: Duplicate UniqueIdentifier refused when a service is saved in the editor
cases.what: The service editor refuses to save a service whose UniqueIdentifier is already used by another service, and template loading renames a clashing identifier.

cases.case: Duplicate UniqueIdentifier refused on every path that publishes
cases.what: Cloning gives the copy a new UniqueIdentifier, and publishing from the editor or the configuration API and restoring a saved copy all refuse two published services with the same UniqueIdentifier; a disabled copy, which is not published, is accepted.

noted: A configuration file edited outside the server that already repeats a UniqueIdentifier is loaded and served as it is, with a warning in the log, until its next publish is refused.

requirements.name: Subscription packages

cases.case: SubscriptionPackage on service instances
cases.what: Emits the operator's package label as a SubscriptionPackage in every ServiceInstance of the service, in schema order after Availability.

cases.case: SubscriptionPackageList when packages are used
cases.what: Writes a SubscriptionPackageList after the services listing once each package carried on a service instance, and none when no instance carries one.

noted: Only one package label per service is possible, applied identically to all its instances; packages are never attached to LCN tables.

requirements.name: Service and service list identifiers

cases.case: ServiceList@id
cases.what: Uses the configured list identifier, or a tag: URI by default, and keeps it the same whatever query parameters the request carries.

cases.case: Service UniqueIdentifier
cases.what: Emits the configured identifier; the editor proposes a tag: URI when the operator leaves it empty.

noted: The default identifiers use the reserved example domain dvbi.example as tagging entity, so every deployment that keeps the defaults publishes the same identifiers; an operator-entered identifier is not checked for a URI scheme when saved (only the editor's separate checker warns).

requirements.name: Linked applications in the service list

cases.case: HowRelated from LinkedApplicationCS:2019 and MediaUri with @contentType
cases.what: Emits a service-level RelatedMaterial with HowRelated urn:dvb:metadata:cs:LinkedApplicationCS:2019:1.1 and a MediaUri whose @contentType is the operator's value or text/html.

cases.case: At most one 1.1 or 1.2 application per @contentType
cases.what: At most one linked application can be configured per service, so at most one such RelatedMaterial is emitted.

noted: The HowRelated term is fixed at 1.1 (application with media in parallel); an application that controls media presentation (1.2), one for when the service is not active (2) or a home page application (3) cannot be signalled.

requirements.name: Part-time services (Availability)

cases.case: Availability inside the service instance
cases.what: When the operator sets a start or end date, every ServiceInstance of the service carries Availability with one Period whose @validFrom and @validTo are those dates.

noted: Only one date window per service can be expressed: no Interval (days of week, times of day, recurrence) and no per-instance difference.

requirements.name: Logos and banners

cases.case: Service logo RelatedMaterial (HowRelatedCS:2021:1001.2, MediaUri with @contentType)
cases.what: Emits one RelatedMaterial per service with HowRelated urn:dvb:metadata:cs:HowRelatedCS:2021:1001.2 and one MediaLocator whose MediaUri carries a @contentType, written only for a JPEG or PNG logo.

cases.case: At least one logo as image/jpeg or image/png
cases.what: A service logo is signalled only when it is image/jpeg or image/png (from the file extension, or the media type of a data URL), uploads accept PNG and JPEG only, and the generated placeholder is not signalled, so every signalled logo is JPEG or PNG; a service without such a logo has no logo RelatedMaterial, which tables 14 and 15 allow.

noted: The logo @contentType comes from the media type of a data URL or from the file extension; a logo URL without a recognised extension is not signalled. No out of service image (1000.1) or content finished image (1000.2) can be signalled.

No service list logo (HowRelatedCS:2021:1001.1), content guide source logo (1002.1) or service banner (1001.3) can be configured or emitted. Clauses 5.2.6.1, 5.2.6.3 and 5.2.6.4 say how each is signalled when it is provided, and RelatedMaterial is optional in tables 14 and 15, so leaving them out is not a departure.

requirements.name: Image requests (variants and width)

cases.case: image_variant validated, 400 for a value not in table 8
cases.what: Every request, on every route including static files, is checked before it is answered: an image_variant outside table 8, or given more than once, gets 400, and a table 8 value is accepted.

cases.case: Only the requested variant returned
cases.what: No image variants exist, so a request naming a valid variant gets the service list without service logos and guide responses without programme images; the default image is not returned in their place.

noted: Uploaded logos are served as stored files, so neither variants nor scaling apply to them either.

The logo endpoint ignores the w parameter and returns a fixed-size SVG, so it neither scales nor rejects a width. Clause 5.2.8.3 places the scaling and 400 obligations on a Content Guide Server, and the text does not say whether they bind the server of a logo referenced from a service list, so no verdict is given here.

requirements.name: Extensibility (ExtensionBaseType)

cases.case: OtherDeliveryParameters carries @extensionName
cases.what: The one OtherDeliveryParameters it emits, for HLS, carries @extensionName and an xsi:type naming the concrete type.

noted: 5G Broadcast is not carried through this extension point: a 5G Broadcast instance is IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters, a TS 103 770 element (see ServiceInstanceType and delivery parameters).

requirements.name: Multilingual elements

cases.case: Each repeated ServiceName carries @xml:lang
cases.what: When the operator gives names in several languages, every ServiceName is emitted with @xml:lang; otherwise a single ServiceName without it.

cases.case: Each element repeated at most once per language code
cases.what: Publishing refuses a service whose name rows have an empty language code or repeat one, so each ServiceName appears once per language code; the editor still lets such rows be entered, and the publish then fails with the reason.

noted: Language codes are compared exactly as entered, so two codes differing only in letter case are both accepted; whether they count as one language code is not judged here (the language tag specification was not opened).

requirements.name: ServiceList fields

cases.case: Name, ProviderName, @id, @xml:lang and schema order
cases.what: Emits Name, ProviderName, LanguageList, RegionList, LCNTableList, ContentGuideSourceList, the services and SubscriptionPackageList in schema order, with @id, @version and @xml:lang; the lists the repository's schema test generates validate against the V1.2.1 schema file (T1).

cases.case: @version incremented for every published change
cases.what: Every path that publishes (editor or API save, logo upload, logo removal, restoring a saved copy) sets @version to the last published number plus one.

cases.case: LanguageList lists the audio languages of the services
cases.what: LanguageList is built from each service's configured audio languages and left out when none is configured.

noted: No TestService is ever emitted, and no service list level RelatedMaterial or TargetRegion.
The element is emitted as LCNTableList, as clause 5.5.1 and the schema file dvbi_v6.0.xsd name it; annex A.1 as printed names it LCNTableTable. Syntax is judged against the schema file.

How services are linked to a content guide source (ContentGuideSourceRef, ContentGuideServiceRef) and the language of the ContentGuideSource ProviderName are judged once, under the Content guide feature.
A list edited by hand outside the server is not given a new @version until its next publish.

requirements.name: Service fields

cases.case: UniqueIdentifier, ServiceName, ProviderName, ServiceType, ServiceGenre in schema order
cases.what: Emits each Service with UniqueIdentifier, its instances, TargetRegion, ServiceName, ProviderName, RelatedMaterial, ServiceGenre, ServiceType, ContentGuideSourceRef and ParentalRating in schema order; ServiceType takes linear, linear-radio, ondemand or data, all terms of DVBServiceTypeCS-2019 (clause D.4); the lists the repository's schema test generates validate against the V1.2.1 schema file (T1).

cases.case: Service@version incremented for every published change
cases.what: Every publish compares each service's rendered element with the one last published; a changed service, or one whose logo file was replaced or removed, gets a higher @version, an unchanged one keeps its number, and a restored copy never goes back to a lower one.

cases.case: ProviderName carries @xml:lang (should)
cases.what: Emits the service ProviderName with @xml:lang set to the list's language, since the provider name is configured in one language only.

noted: ServiceGenre uses the urn:tva:metadata:cs:ContentCS:2011 scheme, which table 15 allows. Whether its term identifiers exist is unverified: could not obtain ETSI TS 102 822-3-1 (TV-Anytime), which defines ContentCS; it is not among the V1.2.1 attachments, and the repository's own term check also leaves ContentCS unchecked. The code maps children to the entertainment term for want of a children term. DVBContentSubjectCS-2019 (clause D.5), the third allowed scheme, is held but not used.

requirements.name: LCN tables

cases.case: LCN entries reference services of this list
cases.what: Each LCN carries the service's channel number and a @serviceRef equal to its UniqueIdentifier, for enabled services only, sorted by number.

cases.case: One table in total when no TargetRegion is used
cases.what: A list without regional services gets a single LCNTable without TargetRegion.

cases.case: One applicable table per TargetRegion
cases.what: With regional services, each region's table numbers that region's services and those targeting no region, and no table without TargetRegion is written, so each region has exactly one applicable table.

noted: A service has one channel number and at most one target region. The editor refuses two services with the same channel number even when they target different regions.

requirements.name: Service parental rating

cases.case: ParentalRating with one MinimumAge applying to all countries
cases.what: When a rating is set, emits ParentalRating with a single MinimumAge and no @countryCodes, which applies irrespective of the country.

noted: Nothing checks the MPD for AdaptationSet.Rating, which, when present, obliges Service.ParentalRating to be signalled and to be at least as restrictive.

requirements.name: Region list

cases.case: RegionList present when services have target regions
cases.what: Emits a RegionList with one Region per distinct service TargetRegion whenever any enabled service has one; TargetRegion values are the regionID as element text.

cases.case: Regions are leaves and selectable
cases.what: Every region is a top-level region without sub-regions and without @selectable, so each is selectable.

cases.case: @countryCodes lists the countries of each top-level region
cases.what: @countryCodes is the list's configured country list (ISO 3166 alpha-3 format checked), never derived from the region identifier, and publishing regional services without it is refused.

cases.case: RegionList@version incremented for every published change
cases.what: RegionList@version is written from the list @version, which every publish increments, including restoring a saved copy.

noted: Table 38 marks CountryRegionType @countryCodes as Optional, while the RegionListType schema in clause 5.6.2.2 and dvbi_v6.0.xsd declare it required. The provider always emits it, which satisfies both. Top-level regions may also be geographical areas rather than single countries (clause 5.6.2.1).

Every region carries the same configured country list, so a list whose regions lie in different countries cannot describe them separately. A configuration file edited outside the server with regional services and no country is served with Region elements without @countryCodes, which the schema rejects, and a warning in the log.

requirements.name: Server-side region selection

cases.case: Full list when the client supplies no information
cases.what: A request without query parameters returns the whole list with its RegionList and no @responseStatus.

cases.case: Postcode or regionID method
cases.what: Supports the regionID method: ?region=<regionID> returns the list tailored to that region (its services and those targeting no region, its Region and its LCN table). The postcode method is not offered, which the clause allows when regionID is supported.

cases.case: @responseStatus on a tailored response
cases.what: A region request is answered with @responseStatus OK, ERROR_INVALID_REGION_ID for a region the list does not define, or ERROR_INVALID_REQUEST for an empty or repeated region, the two error responses carrying the untailored list.

noted: The server's own TargetCountry parameter still tailors the list by matching the start of each service's region identifier; it is not a method of clause 5.6.4 and its responses carry no @responseStatus.
Declaring SRSSupport is left to the registry's ServiceListOffering, which is where clause 5.6.4.1 places it (a contradiction recorded in the specification notes); not judged here.

requirements.name: Service list updates

cases.case: Checks for an update at least every 24 hours (should)
cases.what: Polls the installed list no more often than every 30 seconds and not before its max-age has passed, with If-Modified-Since, and reloads it when its @version changes; it also checks the list once every 24 hours. After a 400 or 406 answer no further request is sent, as clause 4.3.3.2 requires.

cases.case: Randomises an update around a fixed time (should)
cases.what: The daily check runs at a time of day drawn at random over the 24 hours from start-up, then every 24 hours, so clients do not share a fixed update time.

noted: The polling interval follows max-age where the response gives one, with 30 seconds as the minimum; the caching and retry rules of clause 4.3 are judged under their own feature.

requirements.name: ServiceList and Service fields presented

cases.case: Service list Name shown
cases.what: Shows the list's Name as the list title and its @version in settings.

cases.case: TestService not selectable (should)
cases.what: Only Service elements are read, so TestService entries never appear in the channel list.

cases.case: Missing ServiceType means linear television
cases.what: A service without ServiceType is taken as linear television and shown as Linear TV in the player overlay.

noted: Among several ServiceName elements it shows the one without @xml:lang, else the first, whatever the user's language. ServiceRestriction, read for a subscription badge, is not an element of the V1.2.1 schema.
How a service finds its content guide source, and the instance DisplayName, are judged once, under the Content guide and Service instance selection features.

ProminenceList is not read; channel order follows channel numbers and favourites only. Clause 5.2.11 leaves how prominence is shown to local regulation, and its one should (use the nearest ancestor region) applies only to a client that interprets prominence.

requirements.name: LCN tables and channel numbers

cases.case: Table without TargetRegion applies anywhere
cases.what: With no region chosen, or no table for the chosen region, channel numbers come from the table without TargetRegion.

cases.case: Table chosen by the selected region
cases.what: Selects the table whose TargetRegion names exactly the regionID the user chose; tables for other regions are not used.

cases.case: A single table selected, tables not combined
cases.what: Selects one table for the chosen region (and subscription packages), else the one without constraints, and numbers services from that table alone; tables are never combined.

cases.case: @visible=false services left out of normal navigation (should)
cases.what: Reads @visible; a service whose number entry has it false is left out of the channel list, the channel up and down order and the guide grid.

cases.case: Direct entry of the channel number
cases.what: Typing digits selects the service with that channel number: a hidden service is reached this way unless @selectable is false, and other services among those shown under the current filters.

cases.case: @selectable honoured for hidden services (should)
cases.what: Reads @selectable; a service with @visible false and @selectable false is not reached by direct entry of its number, and the flag is ignored for visible services.

cases.case: LCNRange mapping for services without an LCN
cases.what: Services the selected table does not number get numbers from its LCNRange elements in document order, by priority then lowest @start, with both fill methods, ascending, descending and open ranges, and the @serviceType and @serviceGenre filters, for the dvbi and any origins.

noted: Services that neither an LCN entry nor an LCNRange of the selected table numbers get no channel number, which clause 5.5.29 leaves to the client. The deprecated table-level SubscriptionPackage is still honoured when selecting the table.
The region is matched as an exact regionID; the region hierarchy of the RegionList is not used, so a table for a parent region is not selected for a sub-region.

requirements.name: Service target regions

cases.case: Services without TargetRegion shown in every region
cases.what: With a region chosen, the channel list keeps services that have no TargetRegion together with those whose region matches.

cases.case: All TargetRegion elements of a service considered
cases.what: Reads every TargetRegion of a service; it is shown when any one of them is the chosen region.

noted: The region is typed as a regionID and compared exactly; the RegionList (names, hierarchy, @selectable, postcodes) is not read, and clause 5.6.3, which describes region selection, is informative.

requirements.name: Linked applications

cases.case: Application recognised from HowRelated and MediaUri
cases.what: Takes each RelatedMaterial of a service or service instance whose HowRelated is a LinkedApplicationCS:2019 term and keeps the term, the MediaUri and its @contentType as a linked application.

cases.case: Media presented in parallel with an application with media in parallel (1.1)
cases.what: Playback starts on selection independently of any application; the playing instance's 1.1 application is offered from a toolbar button once it has been resolved, an XML AIT read included, and opened in a new window.

cases.case: No media presented for an application controlling media (1.2)
cases.what: For a 1.2 application it plays no media and ignores the instance's delivery parameters: one of a type it can start (an HTML page or an XML AIT) is shown in a frame in the player; one of any other type is kept as the instance's application and the instance is discarded, so its delivery parameters are never played.

cases.case: Instance-level application overrides the service-level one
cases.what: Builds the applications of each instance from its own RelatedMaterial first: an instance-level 1.1 or 1.2 replaces service-level 1.1 and 1.2 of the same @contentType, an instance-level 2 replaces a service-level 2 of the same type, and term 3 is used only at service level.

cases.case: Application signalling of the fallback instance processed
cases.what: When playback falls back to another instance, the applications of that instance are used: its own 1.1 application is offered, and a 1.2 application presents it.

noted: The application URL is opened with an added sid parameter carrying the client's own session identifier and no launch location. Clause 5.2.3.1 says the context of invocation may be passed and, for broadcast-independent HbbTV applications, refers to ETSI TS 102 796 (not opened in this audit), so the launch location sentences are not judged here.

The LinkedApplicationCS terms are told apart: 1.1 is offered from the toolbar, a service-level term 3 application is offered there when the instance has no 1.1, 1.2 presents the service, and 2 is started when the service is off air. A 1.1 application is only opened on request, never started automatically.

Applications of a type other than an HTML page or an XML AIT are ignored, which clause 5.2.3.1 permits, except an application controlling media presentation, which is kept so that its instance is discarded.

requirements.name: XML AIT for linked applications

cases.case: XML AIT (application/vnd.dvb.ait+xml) processed to choose the application
cases.what: Fetches the XML AIT and starts, from its URLBase and applicationLocation, the application with the highest priority whose type is text/html or application/xhtml+xml; the platform profile in mhpVersion is not checked, and HbbTV applications are never chosen as this client has no HbbTV engine, while clause 5.2.4.2 makes the type and the platform profile together decide the application.

cases.case: No error when the XML AIT has no executable application
cases.what: No error is issued: when the XML AIT of an application controlling media presentation holds no application it can start, that instance is discarded and the next one tried, and when none is left the service is shown as unavailable; an application offered beside the media is offered only once its XML AIT gives one it can start, and otherwise is not offered at all, so for it nothing is shown as unavailable, while the clause asks that a service or content item be shown as unavailable.

noted: Content guide deep links (ProgramURL, AuxiliaryURL, Template XML AIT) are left to the content guide feature.

requirements.name: Selection outside scheduled service hours

cases.case: Application started outside scheduled hours (should)
cases.what: When a service is selected outside the scheduled hours of all its instances, or all its instances become unavailable while it plays, the off-air message is shown and the service-level application for an inactive service (LinkedApplicationCS term 2) is started in a frame in the player when its type is one this client can start.

noted: No out of service image (HowRelatedCS:2021:1000.1) is shown; clause 5.2.5.3 lists it as one option among others.

How the client evaluates Availability per instance is judged once, under Service instance selection (clause 5.2.13); the sentences of clause 5.2.5.2 that define the union of Periods describe the signalling and carry no separate client obligation.

requirements.name: Service logos

cases.case: Service logo taken from HowRelatedCS:2021:1001.2
cases.what: Shows the MediaUri of the first RelatedMaterial whose HowRelated is the service logo term.

cases.case: Unavailable image handled
cases.what: A logo that fails to load is hidden and the channel entry still renders.

noted: Among several MediaLocator elements the first is used, whatever its @contentType; no image_variant or width is requested. The logo term is recognised by the text 1001.2 anywhere in HowRelated@href.

requirements.name: Playlists and end of content

cases.case: Manifest fetched only on selection (should)
cases.what: The MPD of an instance, or its DVB-I Playlist document, is requested only when that service is selected and the instance is tried.

cases.case: Content finished image at the end (should)
cases.what: When a VoD MPD, or the last entry of a playlist, has played out, the content finished image (HowRelatedCS:2021:1000.2) of the instance, else of the service, is shown, in the preferred language where there is one, else the first JPEG or PNG.

noted: A DASHDeliveryParameters URI whose UriBasedLocation @contentType is application/xml is fetched as a DVB-I Playlist and its PlaylistEntry MPDs are played in order; a playlist that cannot be fetched or has no entry, or an entry that fails, fails the instance and the next one is tried. Clause 5.2.7.2 says a client can tell the two apart and table 105 marks no Playlist field as required, so this is not a verdict.

requirements.name: Parental rating of services

cases.case: Service.ParentalRating enforced when a threshold and a PIN are set
cases.what: Selecting a service rated at or above the chosen threshold asks for the PIN before playing, and the channel list marks it as locked.

cases.case: Service.ParentalRating enforced when only a threshold is set
cases.what: A threshold chosen without a PIN blocks a service rated at or above it, with a message saying it is blocked and that a PIN unlocks it.

cases.case: MinimumAge for the user's country
cases.what: Uses the MinimumAge whose @countryCodes includes the user's country, else one without @countryCodes; the country is the one last entered for a registry lookup, and with none the most restrictive MinimumAge is applied.

cases.case: Content guide rating takes precedence during its programme
cases.what: When the content guide gives a rating for the programme on air, that rating decides whether selecting the service is allowed, in either direction; otherwise the service rating does.

noted: While a service plays, the programme rating is checked again at each programme change (clause 6.10.15, judged under the content guide feature).

requirements.name: Subscription packages

cases.case: Instance selectable only with a matching package
cases.what: The user chooses the packages the client is associated with in settings, from the list's SubscriptionPackageList, remembered per list @id; an instance whose SubscriptionPackage names none of them is discarded, so the service plays another instance or reports why it cannot play.

noted: With @allowNoPackage false and no package chosen, settings open with a warning asking for one; the list still installs. Clause 5.1.5 lets the package be chosen by the user.

requirements.name: Service list updates

cases.case: Periodic update check (should)
cases.what: No code in this repository checks for, or applies, a service list update.

requirements.exists: The wrapper downloads one fixed external service list into the app cache when it starts and never reads it; the channel list is shown by an external, third-party DVB-I frontend in a WebView, which is not 5G-MAG code, and the wrapper only passes the stream URL the frontend requests to ExoPlayer.

requirements.name: LCN tables and channel numbers

cases.case: LCN table selected
cases.what: No code in this repository parses the service list or its LCN tables.

requirements.exists: The wrapper downloads one fixed external service list into the app cache when it starts and never reads it; the channel list is shown by an external, third-party DVB-I frontend in a WebView, which is not 5G-MAG code, and the wrapper only passes the stream URL the frontend requests to ExoPlayer.

requirements.name: Parental rating of services

cases.case: Service.ParentalRating enforced on selection
cases.what: No code in this repository reads Service.ParentalRating or gates playback.

requirements.exists: The wrapper downloads one fixed external service list into the app cache when it starts and never reads it; the channel list is shown by an external, third-party DVB-I frontend in a WebView, which is not 5G-MAG code, and the wrapper only passes the stream URL the frontend requests to ExoPlayer.

features.name: Service instance selection and delivery
features.summary: The browser client selects instances by clause 5.2.13: per-instance availability, re-evaluation when hours change or an application exits, and @priority with its default of 0; it reads every DRM and CA system, shows DisplayName, caches and makes conditional requests, does not retry 400 or 406, backs off at random and fetches plain HTTP endpoints with a warning, not only on the same private subnet. It does not yet check codecs or the encryption scheme in advance, and after a 401 or 403 has no credentials to present. The provider writes schema-valid delivery signalling, including a 5G Broadcast instance as IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters, and serves over TLS when a certificate is configured, otherwise plain HTTP with a warning. No component implements MBMS carriage (clause 9.3): the client checks and shows the 5G Broadcast signalling, but nothing calls an MBMS Client. The Exo wrapper leaves selection to an external frontend.

requirements.name: HTTP requests and responses for service list access

cases.case: If-Modified-Since on a repeated service list request
cases.what: Every service list, registry and guide request goes through one HTTP client that keeps the Last-Modified time of each document and sends it as If-Modified-Since on the next request for it; the proxy now forwards the header upstream, passes Last-Modified back and relays a 304, which keeps the cached copy.

cases.case: If-Modified-Since omitted when no Last-Modified is held
cases.what: Leaves the header out when no Last-Modified time is held for that URL, which is the case after a page reload, since the times are kept in memory only, and after a response without Last-Modified.

cases.case: Cache-Control max-age honoured
cases.what: Reads Cache-Control max-age on every response, answers a repeated request from its local copy while it is fresh, and polls the current list no sooner than the later of 30 seconds and the end of max-age; the proxy passes the header on. The daily check and any reload go through the same cache.

cases.case: If-None-Match where the server provides an ETag
cases.what: The HTTP client used for every DVB-I request keeps the ETag of each response and sends it as If-None-Match on the next request for that document, omits it when none is held, and takes a new ETag from a 304; the proxy forwards If-None-Match upstream and passes ETag back.
cases.locator: clause 4.3.2.1, referring to ETSI TS 102 796 V1.8.1 clause 7.3.2.6

cases.case: 400 (Bad Request) or 406 (Not Acceptable): no retry of the same request
cases.what: After a 400 or 406 the same request is never sent again in this session: the first load moves to the next listed URI, and the periodic refresh stops for that list.

cases.case: 401 (Authentication Required) or 403 (Forbidden) on a service list: next listed URI
cases.what: Any response other than 2xx or 304, 401 and 403 included, makes the client try the next ServiceListURI of the offering.

cases.case: 401 or 403: wait for Retry-After, then present credentials again
cases.what: After a 401 or 403 the client does not send the request again before the Retry-After period has passed, but it holds no credentials and has no authentication method, so the next attempt is the same unauthenticated request; the clause requires an attempt to re-authenticate after the wait.

cases.case: 404 (Not Found) on a service list: next listed URI
cases.what: A 404 on one ServiceListURI makes the client try the next one listed for the same service list.

cases.case: 404 and no service list acquired: notify the user (should)
cases.what: When every URI fails on first load the channel list shows "Load failed" with the HTTP status and the reason the proxy gives; when a refresh fails it keeps the current list and says so; a failed registry query shows "SLR lookup failed".

cases.case: 500, 502, 504 or connection failure on a service list: next listed URI
cases.what: A server error, or a connection failure, which the proxy reports as 502, makes the client try the next ServiceListURI.

cases.case: Retries no faster than the back-off mechanism
cases.what: After a 500, 502, 504 or a connection failure the client sends no request for that document before the back-off wait has passed, whatever triggers it (periodic refresh, daily check, reload or user action); the periodic refresh waits exactly until then.

cases.case: Back-off: random wait between minwait and maxwait
cases.what: Waits a random period between 4^(CurrentRetry-1) x 100 ms and 4^CurrentRetry x 100 ms, CurrentRetry being 1 after the first failure, rising by one per failed retry, held at 10 (at most 104 857 600 ms) and reset by a success or a page reload; this matches the prose of the clause (up to 400 ms before the first retry, up to 1 600 ms before the second).

cases.case: Redirect followed by 4xx or 5xx: request deemed failed
cases.what: Redirects are followed by the browser for same-origin requests and by the proxy for others, which checks the address of every hop and relays the final status, so a redirect ending in a 4xx or 5xx counts as a failure and the next URI is tried.

noted: A Service List Registry query is sent once per user action; it goes through the same HTTP client, so caching, If-Modified-Since and the retry waits apply, but a failed query is not retried automatically.
After every URI of a list fails on first load the client does not retry automatically; the periodic refresh starts only once a list has loaded.

Besides the periodic refresh, the client checks the current list once a day at a time drawn at random, through the same HTTP client, so a list still fresh by its max-age is not requested; the daily update check of clause 5.1.7 is judged under Service lists.
After a 404 or another failure that clause 4.3.3 gives no rule for, the periodic refresh applies the back-off wait as well, a client choice.

Clause 4.3.2.1 says "The DVB-I client shall follow the cache control requirements in clause 7.3.2.6 of ETSI TS 102 796"; reference [21] is undated and V1.8.1 is the issue held. That clause also asks for the HTTP/1.1 caching rules in general and for an HTTP cache for content accessed by the browser; only max-age and the two conditional headers are judged here.

requirements.name: HTTP over TLS (client)

cases.case: Service list, registry and guide requests over TLS
cases.what: Fetches http:// endpoints as well as https://: each plain HTTP request the proxy makes, redirect hops included, is logged with a warning saying whether the endpoint is on the host's own private subnet, and a service list loaded over plain HTTP is shown with a warning; but plain HTTP is fetched whether or not the endpoint is on that subnet, while the clause allows HTTP without TLS only in that case, and the default service list is http://. Fetching plain HTTP with a warning follows an owner decision.

cases.case: Client supports TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2
cases.what: Relies on the browser for same-origin requests and on Node.js fetch in the proxy for the rest; Node.js allows TLS 1.2 to TLS 1.3 by default (observed on Node.js 24.19.0 in the first pass; the container image uses Node.js 22, not checked).

noted: The client server itself listens on plain HTTP unless a key and certificate are configured, and falls back to HTTP if they cannot be read; that hop is between the browser and the client's own server, not a DVB-I metadata endpoint.

A plain-HTTP endpoint on a private address, the only case the clause allows, is still refused by the proxy's private-address guard unless its origin is named in PROXY_ALLOW_ORIGINS, while one on a public address is fetched; same-origin requests are made by the browser directly and are not logged.

Clause 7.3 takes root certificates, cipher suites, signature algorithms, key sizes and elliptic curves from clause 11.2 of ETSI TS 102 796, now held as V1.8.1; the proxy uses the Node.js defaults and that profile is not judged here.

requirements.name: Service instance precedence

cases.case: Select one instance by precedence, and fall back on error
cases.what: Starts the first instance by precedence when a service is selected and, when the player reports a non-recoverable error, sets that instance aside and applies precedence again to the rest.

cases.case: Instances outside their scheduled service hours not evaluated
cases.what: Availability is read per instance, every Period and Interval, and an instance outside its own scheduled hours is left out before the ranking; a service is shown off-air only when every instance is outside its hours. How Availability itself is read is judged under Service lists (Part-time services).

cases.case: Re-evaluate when an instance enters or leaves its scheduled hours
cases.what: While a service is selected, a timer fires at the next instant any of its instances enters or leaves its scheduled hours and applies precedence again, switching instance when another now comes first, and showing off-air or restarting the service when all or one comes on air.

cases.case: Discard instances whose application controlling media presentation cannot be started
cases.what: An instance whose application controlling media presentation cannot be started is discarded and the next one tried: one of a type the client has no engine for (NOTE 1 i)), an XML AIT with no application it can start, or a URL that cannot be opened; when none is left the reason is shown. The client has no setting to disable an application engine, so NOTE 1 ii) does not arise.

cases.case: Discard instances that can be known in advance not to play
cases.what: Before trying an instance, leaves out multicast delivery, DASH or HLS when no player for it is available, conditional access only, DRM when the browser has no Encrypted Media Extensions, and DRM systems the player knows no key system for. It does not read the codecs or picture format an instance signals in ContentAttributes, nor check @encryptionScheme, so an instance whose codec, format or scheme the browser cannot play is set aside only after playback fails.

cases.case: Re-evaluate when an application controlling media presentation exits
cases.what: An application controlling media presentation runs in a frame in the player; closing the frame, which is how such an application exits here, discards its instance and applies precedence again, so the next instance plays.

cases.case: ServiceInstance@priority respected
cases.what: Orders the remaining instances by ascending @priority, lower value first, and tries them in that order; equal priorities keep document order.

noted: Clause 5.2.1 (service instance matching) binds hybrid clients with DVB-T/C/S tuners. This browser client has none, so matching does not apply; it marks a service whose instances are all DVB-T/S/C as broadcast only.

When every instance fails, the message lists the reasons instances were discarded in advance; when there are none and any instance carries ContentProtection, it says the stream is DRM protected and no CDM is available, whatever the actual cause.
Instances outside the subscription packages the user has chosen are also discarded before ranking; subscription packages are judged under Service lists.

How the client reads Availability (Period, Interval, per instance) and how it handles applications controlling media presentation (clause 5.2.3.2) are judged under Service lists; only their effect on instance selection is judged here.

requirements.name: ServiceInstanceType and delivery parameters (client)

cases.case: DisplayName, falling back to ServiceName
cases.what: Reads the first DisplayName of each instance, or the service name when there is none, and shows it in the toolbar and the player overlay while that instance plays; the channel list keeps the service name.

cases.case: @priority default
cases.what: Treats an instance without @priority as priority 0, the schema default and the highest priority.

cases.case: DASHDeliveryParameters/UriBasedLocation
cases.what: Takes the URI from UriBasedLocation and plays it as an MPD with dash.js 5.2.0, or, when @contentType is application/xml, fetches it as a DVB-I Playlist on selection and plays its entries in order; MinimumBitRate and Extension are not used, which table 100 does not require.
cases.locator: clause 5.5.18.6, DASHDeliveryParametersType schema; clause 8.5.3.2, table 100, row UriBasedLocation

noted: MulticastTSDeliveryParameters are parsed into a udp:// address and then discarded before selection, since a browser cannot join multicast; table 86 does not require them of IP-only receivers.

HLS is accepted through OtherDeliveryParameters when @extensionName or xsi:type contains "mpegurl", "m3u8" or "apple" (annex G, informative), and an extension whose name contains "dash" is played as DASH; IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters, RTSPDeliveryParameters, SATIPDeliveryParameters and the deprecated SourceType are ignored.
FTAContentManagement is not read; table 102 marks none of its attributes as required.
SubscriptionPackage is now read per instance and decides which instances can be selected; it is judged under Service lists.

A 5G Broadcast instance (IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters holding an mbms:// locator) yields no playable instance, since a browser has no MBMS Client. The client checks the locator against TS 26.347 clause 8.2.2 and shows it, its priority and its MBMS User Service on a 5G badge, or says what is wrong; another instance of the service plays if one is listed.

An application controlling media presentation (LinkedApplicationCS 1.2, clause 5.2.3.2), for which the client presents no media and ignores delivery parameters, is judged under Service lists (Linked applications).

requirements.name: ContentProtection (client)

cases.case: DRMSystemId: identify that an instance is protected
cases.what: Collects every DRMSystemId of each instance and maps the Widevine, PlayReady, FairPlay and one ClearKey identifier to browser key systems for dash.js and hls.js; an instance protected only by systems with no mapping is discarded before playback.

cases.case: Several DRMSystemId in one ContentProtection
cases.what: Reads every DRMSystemId of each ContentProtection element.

cases.case: CASystemId
cases.what: Reads every CASystemId; an instance protected by conditional access only is discarded, since a browser cannot descramble it.

cases.case: DRMSystemId@encryptionScheme
cases.what: @encryptionScheme is read and kept per DRM system but not acted on: a cbcs or cbcs-10 instance is neither told apart from a cenc one nor checked against the browser before playback. Table 103 marks it as required for IP-only receivers, which must understand and act on it.

noted: A licence server is configured only from a LicenseServerURL element inside ContentProtection, which the V1.2.1 schema does not define; lists from the provider never carry it.

NOTE 3 of clause 8.5.1 (informative) explains that ContentProtection support means identifying whether content is protected and whether the receiver supports the scheme. The client checks for Encrypted Media Extensions and a known key system before playback, but does not query the browser for the key system and scheme; the normative effect, discarding in advance an instance that cannot play, is judged under Service instance precedence.

The client maps ClearKey from urn:uuid:1077efec-c0b2-4d02-ace3-3c1e52e2fb4b, while the provider writes urn:uuid:e2719d58-a985-b3c9-781a-b030af78d30e for ClearKey. TS 103 770 does not define the identifier: table 35 says DRMSystemId values are as described in clause 8.2 of ETSI TS 103 285, which was not obtained, and the schema types the value as a string. Not judged. (Provider line not re-checked in this pass.)

requirements.name: Interoperability point IP1, IP-only mobile receiver: delivery

cases.case: Identify and store the DVB-DASH services of a service list
cases.what: Parses every Service, keeps those with a DASH (or other IP-deliverable) instance, and keeps broadcast-only ones in the list marked as such.

cases.case: Continuous presentation of the selected DVB-DASH stream
cases.what: Plays the selected instance's MPD, or the entries of a DVB-I Playlist in order, with dash.js 5.2.0 and switches to the next instance on a fatal error; whether this meets the DVB-DASH profile requirements of clause 8.5.2 was not checked.

cases.case: Identification of streams with content protection applied
cases.what: Identifies a protected instance from its ContentProtection DRMSystemId and CASystemId values and uses them to configure the player's key systems, to discard instances it cannot play and to word the error shown when every instance fails; the clause asks for identification and does not say it must be shown to the user.

noted: Protected services are not marked in the channel list or the info overlay.
Whether the DASH playback meets the DVB-DASH profiles that clause 8.5.2 requires depends on ETSI TS 103 285, which was not obtained; it is not part of any verdict here.

requirements.name: Carriage in MBMS: DVB-I client behaviour

cases.case: Start reception of the MBMS Service Announcement Channel
cases.what: The client has no interface to an MBMS Client.

cases.case: Acquire the service list from an MBMS User Service when there is no unicast connection
cases.what: The client loads service lists over HTTP only.

cases.case: On selecting an instance with an mbms:// locator, start reception of the MBMS User Service
cases.what: No MBMS User Service is ever started.

cases.case: Pass the entry point document from the User Service Description to the player
cases.what: The player is only given URLs taken from the service list.

cases.case: Subscribe to MBMS Client update notifications for metadata acquired over MBMS, and re-acquire new versions
cases.what: No MBMS Client is used, so no update notifications are subscribed to; this applies once metadata is acquired over MBMS, which does not happen today.

requirements.exists: The client reads the mbms:// locator of a 5G Broadcast instance from IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters, checks it against TS 26.347 clause 8.2.2, and shows it with the MBMS User Service it names; it plays any other instance the service has. A browser has no MBMS Client, so no reception is started.
noted: The repositories carry 5G broadcast (MBMS) delivery in a local extension, urn:5g-mag:metadata:dvbi-5g:2026, inside OtherDeliveryParameters. It is not part of TS 103 770 and is not judged here.

Clause 9.3.3 refers to a service instance with an mbms:// locator, but the document does not say which element carries such a locator. This does not change any case here: the client has no interface to an MBMS Client at all. The procedures of ETSI TS 126 346 and TS 126 347 that the clause cites were not obtained and no verdict depends on them.

requirements.name: HTTP responses for service list access (server)

cases.case: 200 (OK) with the document when changed since If-Modified-Since
cases.what: Answers /service-list.xml with 200, the full list and a Last-Modified header when the configuration was saved after the If-Modified-Since time.

cases.case: Standard GET when no If-Modified-Since is sent
cases.what: A request without the header, or with an unparseable date, always gets 200 and the full list.

cases.case: 401 or 403 only where the endpoint requires client authentication
cases.what: The service list never answers 401 or 403; only the administration routes, which are not DVB-I endpoints, answer 401.

noted: A 304 (Not Modified), which the clause permits, is returned when nothing was saved after the If-Modified-Since time; the comparison uses whole seconds.
The list is sent with Cache-Control: no-cache and no max-age, which clause 4.3.2.1 leaves optional.
One Last-Modified time covers every TargetCountry and region variant of the list, and it is reset to the start time whenever the server restarts.

requirements.name: HTTP over TLS (server)

cases.case: Service list and content guide endpoints served over TLS
cases.what: With a key and certificate configured it serves HTTPS only, and an incomplete or unreadable TLS configuration stops it rather than falling back to plain HTTP. With neither configured, the default, it serves plain HTTP and logs a warning quoting the same-private-subnet exception, but does not check that clients are on its private subnet, while the clause allows HTTP without TLS only in that case; behind a TLS-terminating proxy the endpoint URLs in the list are written as https://. Serving plain HTTP with a warning follows an owner decision.

cases.case: Server supports TLS 1.2 (and should support TLS 1.3)
cases.what: With a key and certificate configured it uses the Node.js https server with its default TLS versions; the repository test makes a TLS 1.2 and a TLS 1.3 handshake and both succeed (the container image's Node.js 22 was not checked).

noted: The proxy mode, which writes https:// endpoint URLs for a TLS-terminating proxy in front, rests on the operator's declaration: the presence of a proxy is not detected.
The TLS profile that clause 7.3 takes from clause 11.2 of ETSI TS 102 796 is not judged (the server sets no cipher suites, certificates or key sizes beyond Node.js defaults).
The container image starts the server with no TLS settings, so as built it serves plain HTTP with the warning.
A per-service content guide URL entered by the operator is written as given, http:// included; it points at another Content Guide Server.

requirements.name: ServiceInstanceType and delivery parameters (service list)

cases.case: ServiceInstance elements valid against the V1.2.1 schema
cases.what: DASH instances, multicast instances and DRM signalling are written in schema order, and lists carrying them validate against the V1.2.1 service list schema.

cases.case: @priority
cases.what: Writes @priority when one is configured and leaves it out (schema default 0) when not; a value that is not a non-negative integer is refused on save and restore.

cases.case: DisplayName
cases.what: Writes a DisplayName for every instance, from the instance label or else the service name.

cases.case: DASHDeliveryParameters/UriBasedLocation
cases.what: Writes UriBasedLocation with contentType="application/dash+xml" and the MPD URL in a URI element of the types namespace.

cases.case: MulticastTSDeliveryParameters/IPMulticastAddress
cases.what: Turns a udp://address:port URL into IPMulticastAddress with the Address and Port attributes the schema requires.

noted: Availability in service instances (clause 5.2.5.2), including that only a date window can be configured, is judged under Service lists (Part-time services).
A multicast URL without a port is written with Port 5004, a value no clause gives.
HLS instances use OtherDeliveryParameters with extensionName "vnd.apple.mpegurl" and the hls:m3u8RefType of annex G, which is informative; the base V1.2.1 schema cannot validate them.

DVB-T, DVB-S, DVB-C, RTSP, SAT>IP and IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters cannot be written, nor AltServiceName, so a list from the provider carries no data for clause 5.2.1 service instance matching; FTAContentManagement and the deprecated SourceType are never written.
Linked applications are always written as LinkedApplicationCS 1.1 (media in parallel), never as an application controlling media presentation.

A 5G Broadcast instance is emitted as IdentifierBasedDeliveryParameters holding its mbms:// URL, which the editor checks against TS 26.347 V18.1.0 clause 8.2.2 and refuses with a 400 when it is not an MBMS URL. Table 16 defines the element as an identifier "in the form of a locator (URL)" for "the relevant delivery system"; no clause names it for MBMS, so using it for MBMS is our reading and is not judged as a separate case.

requirements.name: ContentProtection (service list)

cases.case: DRMSystemId with @encryptionScheme
cases.what: Writes one ContentProtection per configured DRM system, with DRMSystemId as a urn:uuid identifier for Widevine, PlayReady, FairPlay and ClearKey and @encryptionScheme from the editor (cenc, cbcs or cbcs-10, default cenc).

noted: CASystemId and @cpsIndex cannot be configured.
A DRM system name the provider does not know is written verbatim as the DRMSystemId value, and an encryptionScheme set through the configuration API is not checked against cenc, cbcs and cbcs-10.
The licence server URL entered in the editor is not written to the list, which has no element for it.

Which identifier stands for each DRM system is not defined in TS 103 770: table 35 refers DRMSystemId values to clause 8.2 of ETSI TS 103 285, which was not obtained, so the identifiers written are not judged.

requirements.name: HTTP requests and responses for service list access

cases.case: If-Modified-Since on a repeated service list request
cases.what: Downloads the external frontend's service list on every start with a plain GET and keeps no Last-Modified time, so no request is ever conditional; the clause asks for the header whenever the time of the last update is known, and says the Last-Modified time should be held for that.

cases.case: Cache-Control max-age honoured
cases.what: Never reads Cache-Control and downloads the list again each time the start screen is created.

cases.case: 400 or 406: no retry of the same request
cases.what: Any failed download, a 400 or 406 included, is logged and not retried.

cases.case: 404 and no service list acquired: notify the user (should)
cases.what: A failed download only prints a stack trace to the log.

noted: Nothing in the wrapper reads the downloaded file; the external frontend in the WebView fetches its own service list.

requirements.name: HTTP over TLS (client)

cases.case: Service list request over TLS
cases.what: Fetches the service list from a hard-coded http:// URL on a public server and enables cleartext traffic for the whole app; the clause requires TLS except on the same private subnet.

noted: The WebView start page, the external DVB-I frontend, is also loaded over http://.

requirements.name: Service instance precedence

cases.case: Select one instance by precedence, and fall back on error
cases.what: The wrapper does not read service instances; which stream plays is decided by the external frontend.

requirements.exists: The wrapper starts ExoPlayer with the first WebView request whose URL contains .mpd; although .m3u8, .mp4 and .ts are also listed, the check returns after the first entry, so only .mpd URLs are intercepted. A later intercepted URL is ignored while the player is open.

requirements.name: Interoperability point IP1, IP-only mobile receiver: delivery

cases.case: Continuous presentation of the selected DVB-DASH stream
cases.what: Plays the intercepted MPD URL in the ExoPlayer r2.18.2 demo player; whether this meets the DVB-DASH profile requirements of clause 8.5.2 was not checked.

cases.case: Identification of streams with content protection applied
cases.what: No ContentProtection information reaches the wrapper; only a URL is handed to the player.

noted: Whether the playback meets the DVB-DASH profiles that clause 8.5.2 requires depends on ETSI TS 103 285, which was not obtained; it is not part of any verdict here.

requirements.name: Carriage in MBMS: DVB-I client behaviour

cases.case: Start reception of the MBMS Service Announcement Channel
cases.what: The wrapper has no interface to an MBMS Client.

cases.case: Acquire the service list from an MBMS User Service when there is no unicast connection
cases.what: The service list is only downloaded over HTTP.

cases.case: On selecting an instance with an mbms:// locator, start reception of the MBMS User Service
cases.what: Only WebView requests whose URL contains .mpd are intercepted; an mbms:// locator is not handled.

cases.case: Pass the entry point document from the User Service Description to the player
cases.what: The player is only given the intercepted URL.

cases.case: Subscribe to MBMS Client update notifications for metadata acquired over MBMS, and re-acquire new versions
cases.what: No MBMS Client is used, so no update notifications are subscribed to; this applies once metadata is acquired over MBMS, which does not happen today.

features.name: Content guide
features.summary: The provider signals its guide through ContentGuideSourceRef, answers timestamp requests with start and end checked and applied, now_next=true and now_next=window with the structural groups, and programme information by pid, writes the metadata profile including a deep-linked XML AIT for on-demand programmes, and returns both tables, empty, for a service with no events. The client finds guide sources by clause 6.1, makes aligned 12 hour, now/next and pid requests, browses More Episodes and Box Sets with pagination, launches on-demand through the XML AIT and enforces programme ratings; after a 404 from any guide endpoint it re-acquires the service list. The empty Schedule element and the programme image HowRelated term fall under contradictions in the specification. The Exo DVB-I Player leaves the guide to an external frontend.

requirements.name: Content guide source signalling

spec.locator: clause 6.1; clause 5.5.7, table 20; clause 5.5.2, Service table rows ContentGuideSourceRef and ContentGuideServiceRef

cases.case: ContentGuideSourceList with @CGSID
cases.what: Emits a ContentGuideSourceList with one ContentGuideSource for the list, plus one for each service that has its own guide URL, each with a @CGSID that is checked to be a valid xs:ID before the list is saved.

cases.case: ProviderName (mandatory)
cases.what: Every ContentGuideSource carries a ProviderName taken from the configuration (the service name or provider for per-service sources); it has no @xml:lang of its own and inherits the one on ServiceList, where table 20 says it should carry one.

cases.case: ScheduleInfoEndpoint (mandatory) with @contentType application/xml
cases.what: Every ContentGuideSource has a ScheduleInfoEndpoint with contentType="application/xml" and a URI, pointing at the provider's own schedule endpoint or at the operator's per-service guide URL.

cases.case: Service refers to its content guide source with ContentGuideSourceRef
cases.what: Every service carries ContentGuideSourceRef with the CGSID of a source in the list's ContentGuideSourceList: its own source for a service with its own guide URL, otherwise the list's.

cases.case: ContentGuideServiceRef is the identifier used in guide queries
cases.what: No ContentGuideServiceRef is written, so clients query the guide with the UniqueIdentifier, which the schedule, now/next and programme endpoints answer to.

noted: GroupInfoEndpoint, MoreEpisodesEndpoint, Name, RelatedMaterial (logo) and @minimumMetadataUpdatePeriod are never emitted; table 20 makes all of them optional, so the More Episodes, Box Set and pagination rules of clauses 6.7 to 6.9 do not apply to this provider.
No ContentGuideServiceRef is written any more; how the DVB-I Application reads the content guide signalling is judged in its own audit.
The list-level source also signals ProgramInfoEndpoint with contentType application/xml, at the programme information handler; its behaviour is judged under the programme information request.
